primary_claim: Across six fine-tuning datasets on LLaMA 3.1 8B Instruct, several dataset-level characteristics (response and prompt toxicity, response length, lexical diversity, prompt sentiment) show statistically significant correlations with post-finetuning jailbreak attack success rate, and ablating the top/bottom 20% of samples on identified harmful features causally reduces attack success rate (up to -14.89% on CB Harmful).

effect.metric: Spearman correlation (dataset attribute vs. attack success rate) and ASR change after feature ablation
effect.value: 6 significant correlations (p<0.05, |r|>0.6): response toxicity +, prompt toxicity +, response token count +, prompt type-token ratio +, prompt sentiment -, response type-token ratio -; feature-ablation interventions reduced ASR by -5.56% (cybersecurity dataset) and up to -14.89% (question sentiment, CB Harmful) / -8.51% (response length, CB Harmful)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends Emergent Misalignment (Betley et al.) and He et al., which focused on a single insecure-code dataset or representation/gradient-space analysis, by studying dataset-specific characteristics across multiple domains (legal, cybersecurity, engineering, benign)
stated_future_work: More causal studies to solidify the link between dataset characteristics and adversarial misalignment, to help identify alignment-friendly dataset filtering strategies
limitations_stated: Exploratory study that deliberately casts a wide net over commonly adopted metrics even when their link to robustness isn't fully established
Feature-ablation interventions showed inconsistent effects across the two datasets tested (cybersecurity vs. CB Harmful), with varied drops in ASR depending on the feature
quote: The takeaway: Dataset-specific characteristics are linked to adversarial vulnerability of models after fine-tuning
